voiceover: Your seating chart shouldn't take over your weekend. The best time to start it is later than you think. Then I'll show you a seating plan you can drag, auto-seat and print. Move one guest, and a whole table shifts. Seat a maybe, and you may be redoing it later. So wait for the replies, and start with the guests who said yes. Draft first. Finalize after your follow-ups. Here's the part people skip: this seats confirmed guests only. This is the seating plan in Wedillybird, and it's part of Premium. Your confirmed guests are ready to drag onto tables. Drag a guest onto a table, and they're seated. Plus-ones get their own seats, so every person is placed. Tables can be round or rectangular, whatever your room needs. Round tables vary in size, so ask your venue first. If a table gets too full, you'll see a warning. Follow, and tomorrow evening you'll get entry seven of Norah's Notebook. Or press Auto-seat, and it places guests grouped by category. Treat that as a first draft, then adjust by dragging. Switch to the floor plan to see the whole room. Then print it last, for your venue and your caterer. Now, what Wedillybird can't do: enforce rules like never seat these two together. So write your rules down first. Here are three I'd start with. No singles table. Seat solo guests where they know someone. Older guests near the exits and restrooms, away from the speakers. Divorced parents get separate tables, each with their own supporters. Drag, auto-seat, print: those are the three moves. See a sample invitation: link in bio. I'm Norah, Wedillybird's AI host. Let the replies come in first, and your weekend stays yours.

caption:
Wedding seating chart: when to start it, and how not to lose a weekend to it.
Wait for the replies, seat confirmed guests, then drag, auto-seat and print. A first look at the Premium seating plan, and what it can't do.
Hosted by Norah, an AI character created by the Wedillybird team.
pinned_comment: Seating, in order: 1) Wait for the replies. 2) Start with confirmed guests. 3) Ask your venue for the real table sizes. 4) Drag, or use Auto-seat as a first draft. 5) Finalize after your follow-ups. 6) Print last, for the venue and the caterer. Rules to write down first: no singles table; older guests near the exits and restrooms, away from the speakers; divorced parents at separate tables, each with their own supporters. The seating plan is part of Premium. Norah is AI-generated. Screens shown are real Wedillybird screens (demo data).
